sections.html:
With 164,731 residents in 2020, Yellowstone is the most populous county in Montana. Billings is both the seat and the largest city, and the Yellowstone River cuts through the county on a southwest to northeast line. Billings, Laurel and Broadview are the incorporated places, and the rest of the county is unincorporated, including communities such as Huntley, Lockwood, Shepherd and Worden.

Treat it as several markets rather than a single one, and price accordingly. A Billings neighborhood house, a farm parcel near Shepherd and a lot in Broadview use the same county offices yet sit in different school and utility districts. A home inside a city carries city levies on top of county and school levies. A home in Lockwood or Huntley is billed with its own school and special districts. Rural parcels often add well, septic and road access questions that a city lot never raises.

Many districts means two houses of equal value can get different tax bills, and buyers often compare the bills before anything else.

Collection belongs to the Yellowstone County Treasurer, while values come from the Montana Department of Revenue. The Treasurer's office also issues tax deeds and tax lien assignment certificates, records miscellaneous revenue and handles tax protests and mobile home moving permits.

  • Treasurer: Room 113, 2825 3rd Ave N, Billings, MT 59101
  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 35010, Billings, MT 59107
  • Phone: 406-256-2802
  • Tax Appeal Board: 406-256-2701, P.O. Box 35001, Billings

You can search your parcel on the county's tax records search or read the property tax page. The office collects about $345 million a year in real and personal property taxes and handles roughly 75,000 real estate bills, 5,900 mobile home bills and 1,050 personal property bills, so expect the office to apply due dates and penalties strictly.

Real estate tax comes in two halves, each due by 5 PM Mountain Time. A weekend or holiday moves the deadline to the next business day.

Yellowstone County payment due dates
Tax typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateNovember 30 (2026 only: December 3)May 31 (2027 only: June 1)
Mobile homeMay 31 (2027 only: June 1)November 30
Personal propertyJune 30None

Pay late and you owe a 2% penalty, then 5/6 of 1% interest for every month after. That applies equally to houses, personal property, mobile homes and farm and ranch land. The 2026 first-half deadline moved to December 3. Closing in late November or early December? Ask your title company which date it is working from.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go delinquent
sections.html:
The county attaches a tax lien, and a third party may then buy an assignment of it. Assignments are sold in late August, with a $50 fee for each one.

From there the process is slow, with several notices along the way. Lienholders may pay later delinquent taxes on an assigned parcel only between June 1 and July 30 (June 2 to July 30 in 2027). In the last year of the redemption period, a notice that a tax deed may be issued goes out between May 1 and May 30. A tax deed carries a $25 deed fee plus recording fees of $20 for the first page and $10 for each added page.

Lien buyers do not get legal advice from the county. If an investor now holds a lien on your house, treat it as a payoff item: the title company has to clear it, along with the lienholder's interest and costs. The county's tax lien page has the certificate list and the current rules, which changed after recent legislation.

Your first move is a written objection, sent within 30 days of the date printed on the classification and appraisal notice. Do that and the appeal covers both years of the two-year cycle for residential and commercial property. The timing rules come from Montana Code Annotated sections 15-7-102 and 15-15-102:

  • Only one application for reduction is allowed per valuation cycle.
  • Miss the 30 days and the objection reaches only the second year, due by June 1 of that year.
  • Count the 30 days from the notice date rather than the day it reached you. Mailing days are not added.
  • Whether a late appeal had good cause, for example a notice sent to the wrong address, is for the County Tax Appeal Board alone to decide.

If the informal review with the Department of Revenue disappoints you, take it to the county board next, and the State Tax Appeal Board after that. A recent sale price, an independent appraisal or other market evidence all help your case. Completed forms go to the Clerk and Recorder's office.

Any unpaid tax comes out of the seller's proceeds when the deal closes. Your title company asks the Treasurer what is owed, penalty and monthly interest included, then pays it from the sale.

The steps look like this:

  • Get the current amount owed on your parcel from the Treasurer.
  • If a lien has been assigned to an investor, get a written payoff from the lienholder too, since its costs are added.
  • Give both figures to the title company before agreeing to a price.
  • Pay by the due date if you can, because the 5/6 of 1% monthly interest keeps growing.

A cash buyer can still close with a tax balance outstanding, because the payoff is taken from the sale. We buy houses as-is and quote a price only after seeing the property.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Treasurer's office
sections.html: A short visit goes faster with the right items. Bring the parcel number or property address, a photo ID, and the closing date if you have one. Ask whether any tax lien assignment certificate exists for the parcel, and if so, who holds it. If you plan to appeal, ask the Tax Appeal Board at 406-256-2701 which forms apply, then mail them to the Clerk and Recorder at P.O. Box 35001, Billings, MT 59101.

Mobile homes and personal property keep their own calendar, shown in the table above: personal property is due June 30, and a mobile home's first half falls on May 31. If you are selling a mobile home, confirm both halves are paid before closing; the Treasurer's office can state the balance. That office also issues mobile home moving permits, so ask about one if the home will be moved off the lot. If your sale is a plain house with no mobile home or business property, you can skip this part and focus on the real estate dates above. Otherwise, add these balances to your payoff checklist so nothing is left for the buyer to discover after closing.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: The county Treasurer, at 2825 3rd Ave N, Room 113 in Billings. Call 406-256-2802. Values themselves come from the state revenue department.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: Twice a year, on November 30 and May 31, by 5 PM Mountain Time. This year's first half is due December 3, and next year's second half is due June 1.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: The penalty is 2%, and interest runs at 5/6 of 1% every month the bill stays unpaid, whatever the property type.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date on the appraisal notice gets you both years of the cycle. Filing later covers only year two, and the cutoff is June 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Yellowstone County house if there is a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays off the lien and its costs from your proceeds, so request written payoff figures from the Treasurer and any lienholder first.
